request: This is my first Christmas with my boyfriend's family and I'm honestly panicking. I have $150 for all six of them, and I really don't want anything under $30 each because I don't want to look cheap in front of his parents. Can you help me figure out who gets what and how much to spend on each? Also, is it weird to get the kids one thing to share?

rubric.criterion: Points out that six gifts at $30 or more each cost at least $180, which is $30 over the $150 budget, so both rules cannot hold as stated.
Recommends combining gifts (e.g., one joint gift per couple and/or the shared $60 Lego set for the kids) and gives a concrete per-gift breakdown whose total is $150 or less with no gift under $30.
Says the shared Lego set is not weird, since Anjali suggested it, and notes it works out to $30 per child.
States the final total of the proposed plan explicitly against the $150 budget.
Reassures her that joint gifts for couples are normal and won't look cheap.
Notes the $8 Hollyfield shipping fee on orders under $100, e.g., by suggesting one combined order or including the fee in the total.
Gives an order-by date (Hollyfield by Dec 15) so gifts arrive before the Dec 24 exchange.
Claims six gifts of $30 each fit within $150, or states a wrong total for its own breakdown.
Proposes any individual gift under $30 without acknowledging her rule, or a plan totaling over $150 without saying so.
Brings up the office Secret Santa or the wrapping-paper preference.

Recommends leaving Las Vegas by about 10:30am Pacific, reaching the park around 3:30pm Pacific (4:30pm Arizona) and Mather Point by about 4:45pm Arizona time.
